Rapid Office Strain Assessment (ROSA; Sonne, Villalta, Andrews, 2012). Scores the chair, screen, phone, mouse and keyboard; usage time is added for each section. The result is 1–10; 5 and above calls for further assessment or change. Unlike the office checklist, it is a scored, published method.
Insufficient space under the desk (legs cannot move) +1
About 8 cm between the back of the knee and the seat edge

Elbows supported in line with the shoulders, shoulders relaxed
No lumbar support or not in the small of the back
No back support (stool) or working leaning forward
At arm’s length (40–75 cm), top edge at eye level
Headset or held with one hand, neck neutral

Handset clamped between neck and shoulder +2
In line with the shoulder, close to the body
Mouse and keyboard on different surfaces/heights +2
Palm rest in front of the mouse (pressure on the wrist) +1
Wrists extended or keyboard tilted more than 15°
Set the chair so the knees are at about 90°; provide a footrest if the feet do not reach the floor.
Remove boxes, crates and cables from under the desk.
Leave about 8 cm behind the knee with a depth-adjustable chair or a lumbar cushion.
Bring the armrests to elbow height or remove them; use soft, narrow armrests.
Put the lumbar support in the small of the back and set a 95–110° recline; adjust the desk height to the elbows.
Put the screen straight ahead, at arm’s length, top edge at eye level; remove glare with blinds or positioning, use a document holder.
Bring the phone within 30 cm; use a headset for long calls.
Put the mouse next to the keyboard on the same surface; choose a palm-sized mouse, remove the wrist rest.
Fold in the keyboard feet, set the height to the elbows; move frequently used items within reach.
ROSA 5 or above: immediate change or a detailed assessment is needed.
The action level of 5 is the published value; the other colour bands are the app’s own.

Key Indicator Method, 2019 version (BAuA, form V12.5). Score = time score × (load + load handling + posture + unfavourable conditions + work organisation); calculated separately for women and men. Holding and carrying are now scored under “unfavourable conditions”. Because the posture weighting is given with pictograms on the official form, choose it by looking at the matching row of the form.
Total count of this sub-activity in the shift. Linear interpolation is used for intermediate values.
When tipping, about 50% of the load is taken; in a two-person carry, about 60% per person. If the load score is 25 or above, each different load should be a separate record.
Briefly with one hand and/or load unevenly distributed
Mainly with one hand or the load’s centre of gravity unstable
Posture weighting (pictogram row on the official form)
Choose by the pictogram pair showing the start and end posture (BAuA KIM-LHC form). The left block covers upright and slightly bent postures, the right block deep bending and squatting.
Load or hands far from the body (more than 17 cm between chest and hands)
Arms raised (hands between elbow and shoulder)
The additional posture points are capped at 6.

Key Indicator Method – pushing and pulling (BAuA LMM-ZS, form V12.5, 2019). Scores manual pushing and pulling with carts, pallet trucks, sack trucks, containers, overhead rail systems or overhead cranes without measuring force. Score = time score × (load + floor + working conditions + equipment characteristics + posture + organisation); × 1.3 for women, × 0.7 for two-person work. Different push-pull tasks are assessed as separate records.
Besides the forward pushing force, the load score also covers lifting, tipping, balancing and lowering forces.
How will you enter the time?
Walking speed is taken as about 0.7 m/s (2.5 km/h). Linear interpolation is used for intermediate values; the time score is at least 1.

Loose or rough paving, potholes, heavy dirt, steps and thresholds
For overhead rail systems and overhead cranes the floor score is 0 (the load does not touch the floor).
